Sam (acme-dev): Hey team, hitting a regression with JSON/structured output. Previously our price field came back as a number, now it's a string "100" and our downstream parser fails. Not sure if this is model-side or API post-processing.

jamie (support): Thanks for the report Sam — can you paste the exact API request + minimal repro? Also which model and any `json_mode` flags? :eyes:

Sam (acme-dev): Minimal repro: curl to /v1/generate with body:
```json
{
  "model": "open-encoder-3",
  "json_mode": "structured",
  "prompt": "Produce product price json: {\"price\": NUMBER, \"currency\": ENUM(USD,EUR)}"
}
```
Response snippet we get (truncated):
```json
{"product": {"id": 123, "price": "100", "currency": "usd"}}
```
Note `price` is a string, and `currency` lowercased. We used to get 100 (number) and USD. Also seeing `null` for `on_sale` boolean sometimes.

jamie (support): Hmm — could be schema drift in the model output or a change in our structured post-processing. @alex can you check the API post-process logs for that thread id? Sam, do you have a request `request_id`?

Sam (acme-dev): request_id: req_0a9c3f. Happened across 12/15 calls just now.

alex (eng-api): Pulling logs for req_0a9c3f — I see model tokens include `"100"` for the price token. Looks like the model emitted quotes around the number. On our side the structured parser accepts both numeric tokens and numeric-strings but our downstream schema validator is strict (expects number). Was there a model rollout recently?

maria (infra): There was a minor model variant switch in the routing pool at 1812345000 — we routed some low-latency requests to a quantized variant `open-encoder-3-q4`. Could change tokenization/serialization patterns.

jamie (support): So two possible causes: model variant emitting stringified numbers, or our `structured` sanitizer changed. Alex, can you grep commit history for structured-mode serializer in the last 48h?

alex (eng-api): Grepping — no serializer change in API layer. The only change was the routing table (maria mentioned). Also seeing a handful of `SchemaMismatchError: type: number expected, got string` in the validation logs for customers using strict schema enforcement.

jamie (support): Sam — quick mitigation: can you set `tolerant_schema: true` in your SDK call (if available) or post-process by JSON.parse + coercion? We'll follow up with permanent fix.

Sam (acme-dev): I can patch client-side but worried about silent data drift. Ideally we want the platform to guarantee types per schema. Any ETA?

maria (infra): Short term: rolling back a small subset of traffic from `open-encoder-3-q4` to standard variant. Doing a canary now.

support-bot: deploy-bot started rollback of routing pool for model open-encoder-3-q4 -> target 25% -> current 10% :hourglass_flowing_sand:

alex (eng-api): Followup: we'll add a stricter post-validate stage that will either coerce numeric-strings to numbers for known numeric schema fields or surface a clear `SchemaMismatchError` with `field_path` and `raw_value`. That should land in the next patch (ETA ~4 hrs).

jamie (support): Also adding a short KB note on handling numeric-strings and enum casing. Sam — can you share one failing response with the `on_sale` null case? Helps us reproduce boolean/null interplay.

Sam (acme-dev): Pasted another response: `{"product":{"id":124,"price":"99","currency":"EUR","on_sale":null}}` Our schema: `on_sale: boolean` so null breaks validation.

alex (eng-api): Repro confirmed. The model sometimes emits `null` instead of `false`. We're going to implement two fixes: (1) routing rollback (maria) and (2) API-layer coercion for numeric-strings + configurable null-to-false mapping for booleans in structured mode (opt-in for now).

jamie (support): I'll keep Sam updated. If we fix routing and ship the coercion patch, will follow up in a few hours. Sorry for the disruption — this looks like model variant behavior and we should have stricter guarantees. :bow:
__notes: Do not include a title field. Document is one continuous messages string as required.
